BiblicalUsage: Cleanness is the innocency of the hands and the integrity of the heart. Abimelech pleads the innocency of his hands, the psalmist washes his hands in innocency before the altar, Samaria is asked how long before it attains to innocency, and God gives Israel cleanness of teeth — famine — yet they do not return.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe cleanness is proved at the altar: the hands are washed in innocency, and the heart must be as clean as the hands. Samaria is asked how long before it attains to innocency, and God gives cleanness of teeth instead of bread — the famine is the question, asked again.
